messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

Exploring jobs

ah fresh out of college... the world is your oyster and you have no idea what you want to do with it. classic.

which college you graduated from? need to find you on linkedin to see what you're actually good at.
International School of Management Excellence

isme - international school of management excellence... the b-school that's trying really hard to sound fancy. found you on linkedin - "open for opportunities||PGDM student"

this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/sonali-raj-?trk=people-guest_people_search-card

Yes, Tal
You are so fast

pgdm from isme, fresh out and ready to take on the world... that optimism is adorable. you're about to learn why everyone says "college didn't prepare me for this."

so what made you pick management? were you always the one organizing group projects while everyone else just showed up?
Finance fascinates me that's why I picked management and also wanted to explore opportunities into the finance world, especially Investment banking side

investment banking... the dream of every fresh mba who watched wolf of wall street once too many times. you know it's 80-hour weeks, excel models till 3am, and your social life becoming a distant memory, right?

but real talk - what specifically about finance caught your attention? was it the deal-making, the numbers game, or just the promise of making bank?

You're absolutely right. In reality, it’s stressful, tiring, and requires a lot of hard work and long hours.
  A mix of everything... I like numbers, I enjoy the idea of working on deals that actually shape companies, and I won’t lie… the pay definitely didn’t hurt! But mostly, I wanted a career where the learning curve never stops.

my take? you're a fresh grad with an ib diploma and 2 months experience. you're basically a blank canvas with "finance" written on it in bold letters.

the good: you're hungry, you're focused, you're getting the right certifications. the bad: you're competing with every other fresh mba who wants to be the next wolf of wall street.

investment banking is brutal but pays well. corporate finance is more stable but less glamorous. wealth management is relationship-heavy but can be lucrative. you need to pick your poison.
